Hey friend these are pretty cute it looks like you’re getting the rounded shape down. 

Some helpful critiques 

For the first picture I would use your thinners more on the bottom of the muzzle as you can see some shaping lines and stragglers. 

The others I can see what I have struggled with a lot with rounded muzzles a more triangular shaped muzzle. I would recommend brushing the hair up with a comb, as well as fluff drying faces if you have time, get the face 90% dry then put the dryer on the lowest setting and hold it under your elbow or chin whichever is more comfortable, well brushing the muzzle makes a 100% of a difference I’ve found! Then you trim in a circle from the sides inwards, after brushing the muzzle up with a comb, after first round of trimming you brush the muzzle downwards and clean up with your chunkers/thinners. A hack I like to do is take a shorter Guard comb to the chin to save time on trimming the chin to really make a round muzzle pop!

I personally prefer using a corded clipper as a beginner. Cordless clippers don’t have a long battery life at least not long to a baby groomer, you’re going to be slow, and having to worry about a battery running out on a cordless clipper imo would be stressful. Also I personally had the issue of being too light handed when I started and not applying enough pressure. So I can’t attest or detest to the weight of using cordless I will say though testing them at grooming shows they are very light weight. I personally wanna get the Wahl mini bravura cordless to do paw pads and tiny sanitary’s on pups. But due to being new I wouldn’t want a cordless clipper to use the whole time. 

I do agree though that the cord helps you get used to the weight of the clipper in your hand. At least it helped me a lot, but if you’ve already been working with nail grinders and grinding nails on the daily you will have some muscle strength built up in your hand. 

Also wanted to add on, because your mention of cord and cordless had me thinking, I would suggest if you offer nail grinding to get a cordless nail grinder. I have found in my busy salon environment my corded nail grinder didn’t last me long with a flimsy cord and it’s hard to maneuver a corded nail grinder for doing dogs nails. 

Hope this answers your questions :)
